test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What are transverse waves?

options.text: These are the waves which do not require medium for their propagation.
These are the longitudinal mechanical waves.
In these waves, the particles of the medium vibrate in the parallel direction of propagation of the waves.
In these waves, the particles of the medium vibrate perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the waves.

solution:
The correct answer is __**In these waves, the particles of the medium vibrate perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the waves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

Wave motion: 

 
• The type of disturbance that travels through a medium due to repeated vibrations of the particles of the medium about their mean positions is called wave motion.
 
• The sound wave is a kind of mechanical wave.

There are two types of wave motion:

Longitudinal wave motion: 

 
• It is that wave motion in which individual particles of the medium execute simple harmonic motion about their mean position along the same direction, in which the wave is propagated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c3482e4a332245062f3dbc16cc75d2244cabc88c9d8c26e0fd25881bc03f81f.png] 

 
• For example: Sound waves

Transverse wave motion: 

 
• The vibration of particles in a medium and the propagation of waves are perpendicular to each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8c33c4f183faef139202f6518edf8df8078a83d470ee1da137810da41ada9ec.png] 

 
• Example: Waves in the surface of the water, waves in a string, light waves, etc.
